modelingNotes: Eight mapped parts determine the stone halls, glass nave and crossing dome; the highest mapped roof is 50 m.
Opaque cool glazing and muted green framing approximate the glass-and-iron roof without textures or transmission.

Barrel vaults replace the generic round-roof fallback; rib spacing, facade rhythm and a 6 m crossing finial above the mapped dome are original simplified interpretations of reviewed aerial and facade photographs.

modelingNotes: Footprint, 52 freestanding columns, plinth, roof and stair locations use the 63 saved OSM parts.
OSM IGN Lidar HD heights are retained, including the decimal-comma 2.2 m terrace.
Column capitals, cornice bands and dark doorway rhythm are inferred from reviewed daylight exterior photographs.
Stair flights retain mapped slopes; sculpture, fluting and relief carving are omitted at map scale.

assets.name: Opéra Garnier
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The saved OSM footprint and eleven mapped parts control the stepped massing, auditorium dome, side rotundas and fly tower.
Part heights top out at 58 m; the outline tag of 70 m is not used to inflate these more detailed mapped volumes.
Copper green, paired facade columns, cornice bands and gilded finials are simplified interpretations of the reviewed south facade photographs.
Facade openings are shallow opaque recesses. Sculpture groups, medallions and roof ornament are represented by simple accents, not replicas.

assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The saved OSM outline and four courtyard holes are preserved; its 12 m overall height is retained.
OSM has no building parts. The main range is identified along the southern end of the principal courtyard; 9.5 m main eaves and 6 m service-wing eaves are inferred from exterior references.
Mansards and windows are simplified. Interior spaces, gardens, furnishings and security installations are outside the model.

assets.name: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: All 44 mapped part plans and total heights are retained; the north campanile and south entrance remain geographically aligned.
Four 46 m satellite domes lack roof:height in OSM; a 13 m dome above the mapped 33 m drums is inferred from reviewed exterior photographs.
Pale roof material, drum openings, mouldings and small crosses are original simplified visual interpretations.
OSM models the front porch with an enclosing 16 m base: the porch is opened below its mapped 9 m lintel using the mapped porch polygon.
Domes are faceted latitude profiles; sculpture, equestrian figures and fine masonry are omitted.

assets.name: Cathédrale Saint-Alexandre-Nevsky
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The mapped church outline and five tower parts determine placement; part heights of 48 and 24 m take precedence over the 6 m base-building tag.
The reviewed photographs show steep tent roofs with small onion finials. Three metres of each mapped roof height are reserved for simplified gold finials and crosses.
The 6 m enclosing base, arched drum windows and facade rhythm are schematic. Sculpture, mosaics and individual ornamental arches are omitted.

assets.name: Église Saint-Augustin
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The mapped 70 m main dome and raised lantern reaching 83 m dominate the tapered church plan. Smaller cupolas and gabled nave retain mapped heights; arched windows follow actual wall eaves.
Light blue facade panels are clipped to real wall faces before export and checked again in both GLB levels. Window spacing and minor cornices are inferred, not survey measurements.

assets.name: Église Saint-Roch
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The saved footprint and three roof-part outlines control the plan. OSM contains no heights: nave eave 22 m, ridge 29 m and chapel dome top 30 m are provisional visual inferences, requiring height review.
Cross/apse gables are approximated with the shared mapped gable primitive. The lower outline envelope is inferred at 12 m; no courtyard is filled.
The two-storey classical facade is suggested by arched light blue panels and narrow cornices. Columns, sculptures and the portal pediment need a future detail review.

assets.name: Église Saint-Vincent-de-Paul
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Twin 45 m belfries and the stepped nave use the nine saved mapped parts. Slate gables with a 4 m rise are inferred inside existing nave height bounds; bell openings and facade rhythm are schematic. The front 20 m part is opened into a six-column portico; column diameter and 16 m pediment eave are inferred from the reviewed facade.
Light blue facade panels are clipped to real wall faces before export and checked again in both GLB levels. Window spacing and minor cornices are inferred, not survey measurements.
